title: Activists rally in Antalya for climate protection and rights

tea.why: Activists marched to demand climate action and human rights during the COP31 summit in Antalya.
tea.want: A clear roadmap to phase out fossil fuels and greater attention to climate justice.
tea.changed: Nov 14: Thousands marched through central Antalya during the COP31 climate conference.

summary: Thousands of people marched through central Antalya on Saturday, November 14, 2026, during the COP31 climate summit. Organised by environmental and human rights NGOs, labor unions, and political parties, the rally called for urgent climate action and a roadmap to end fossil fuel reliance, criticizing global leaders and COP negotiators for ignoring ordinary citizens. Police estimated the crowd at over 7,000 participants, while organizers stated that more than 10,000 people took part. Police secured the route by checking bags and banners at the entrance to the designated area near Aydin Kanza Park before demonstrators marched to the Republic Square. Authorities did not report any arrests or major incidents during the demonstration, though police inspected banners and flags.
demands: A clear roadmap to exit fossil fuels
Inclusion of citizens' voices in climate negotiations
response: Police secured the demonstration route, checked bags and banners at entry points, and monitored the march. Turkish Environment Minister and summit president Murat Kurum had stated prior to the event that peaceful demonstrations are permitted.

crowd.text: more than 10,000 people according to organizers, while police estimated over 7,000

updates.text: Thousands of protesters gathered at Aydin Kanza Park in Antalya and marched toward Republic Square.
